item.title: Dawn of War 2 review (2009)
item.content:encoded: Space Marines, ding gratz lol.

item.title: We live in a world where every single Hatsune Miku is canon, which means that includes Helldivers Miku and Pyramid Head Miku
item.content:encoded: She's no longer just hiding in your wifi.

item.title: The design lead of Half-Life's biggest competitor says that its publisher was so 'pissed off' by the time the game launched that it didn't bother testing it properly: 'We got trashed in the press because of bugs'
item.content:encoded: "It really hurt it when it came to reviews."

item.title: A game developer compared Godot and Unity by making the same game in both engines, and he's found a clear winner
item.content:encoded: Godot is smaller, faster, and quicker to load than Unity, according to tests run by designer Thomas Grové.

item.title: Space Marine 2 gets a steep discount, a free trial and an update that adds a 'major revamp' of Siege Mode, as its multiplayer continues to outpace games like Marathon
item.content:encoded: The overhaul makes horde sessions "quicker and more intense".

item.title: I can't wait to get murdered by flowers in this rad-looking survival horror game
item.content:encoded: The Florist looks like Resident Evil meets Annihilation.

item.title: Keep your GTA 6, the news I can finally play the console-exclusive DLC for Saints Row 2 from 2009 on PC is what I've been waiting for
item.content:encoded: Bless the modders.

item.title: Jackbox's first externally published game looks like the shot in the arm the stealth genre needs, and it'll be out this year
item.content:encoded: Ha ha, get it, because it's called My Arms Are Longer Now.

item.title: A 23-year-old D&D CRPG just got patched to add achievements and fix a bug that stopped you from earning XP
item.content:encoded: Time to go back to The Temple of Elemental Evil.

item.title: Great moments in PC gaming: Stealing and selling someone else's treasure in Sea of Thieves
item.content:encoded: It's what the pirate life is all about.

item.title: Our readers are clear: They want Destiny 3, which is awkward, because Bungie reportedly isn't making Destiny 3
item.content:encoded: D'oh.

item.title: Kickstarter rolls back new mature content guidelines after week of backlash
item.content:encoded: The crowdfunder's payment processor, Stripe, "can still suspend a campaign that Kickstarter has approved."

item.title: 14 years ago we published our Elder Scrolls 6 wishlist, and honestly? It still holds up
item.content:encoded: Waiting on a hero (named Todd Howard).

item.title: Diablo 2 players made nearly 2 million warlocks in a single month
item.content:encoded: Like the lord of terror himself, Diablo 2 has a remarkably long tail.

item.title: I'll never love another RPG like I loved Neverwinter Nights
item.content:encoded: Let me tell you about the time when I used to build worlds.

item.title: The best birding board game on PC is getting a sequel about dragons, which are like cooler birds
item.content:encoded: Roseate spoonbill son or shaly rockbreaker daughter?

item.title: Deadlock's latest 'small update' yet again remixes basic mechanics and rebalances most of the roster
item.content:encoded: It'll be harder to claim the soul urn without a fight, and the midboss spawns at match start.

item.title: PC Gamer's MMO readers are, according to you, fashion-forward healers who like your keybinds, and I couldn't be more proud
item.content:encoded: MMO to the polls.

item.title: As the UK plunges once more into political chaos, I’ve found the roguelike deckbuilder that can help me process it
item.content:encoded: Prime Monster is a smartly satirical take on the antics of British MPs

item.title: A Broken Sword movie is in the works, aiming to move the adventure game classics into 'the next medium it deserves'
item.content:encoded: Creator Charles Cecil says the emphasis is on 'what Broken sword is' rather than 'what it can be made to look like'.

item.title: The Steam Controller's main competition isn't from Microsoft or Sony: It's from third-party vendors
item.content:encoded: Long gone are the days when third party was for player two.

item.title: You can help save the whales by buying this reef-building game written by the scribe of the Tomb Raider reboot
item.content:encoded: The developer of Life Below is launching a special supporter pack with all net revenue goes to supporting whale and dolphin conservation.

item.title: As it rapidly approaches $1 billion in player funding, Star Citizen goes free to play until May 27
item.content:encoded: No taxation, just representation.

item.title: The director of the best Splinter Cell game reckons that modern lighting engines are making stealth games 'so much harder to read'
item.content:encoded: "It gets very hard to tell what’s light, what’s shadow, what’s dark, what’s safe, what’s dangerous."

item.title: Shock, tears, and relief: How Destiny 2's most popular creators reacted to the end of the legendary shooter
item.content:encoded: "I thought I would be ready to hear something like this, but I guess I'm just not," said popular streamer Datto.

item.title: Last Flag studio lays off half its employees as it puts 'the future of the game in the hands of our players'
item.content:encoded: Night Street Games said earlier this month that it will not be pursuing future development of its CTF shooter.

item.title: Former Bungie dev says 'you'd be surprised how many times' expansions were pitched for a fan-favorite Destiny archvillain who's now left hanging
item.content:encoded: Xivu Arath, we hardly knew ye.

item.title: Fallout lead Tim Cain argues games industry crisis hasn't reached the level of the 1983 crash: 'I don't think there's ever been a worse time in the games industry'
item.content:encoded: He doesn't want to diminish the current crisis, though.

item.title: Why play Wordle when you could be playing this new word puzzle game that rewards you with frogs?
item.content:encoded: It's Ribbit!

item.title: Four years later, Microsoft finally finishes fighting over the Activision acquisition
item.content:encoded: A lawsuit suit, filed by Sjunde AP-Fonden, alleged that the buyout was rushed in order to protect Activision's then-CEO Bobby Kotick.

item.title: EU politician says killing games is bad, but 'wokeness' and the Black samurai Yasuke are the real problem
item.content:encoded: Would you like to watch a neo-fascist embarrass himself in front of the world? I can help.

item.title: Alright, so maybe Zohran Mamdani isn't New York's first gamer mayor
item.content:encoded: It was nice to dream.

item.title: Apple legend Steve Wozniak makes history again: Actually gets applause talking about AI at commencement speech
item.content:encoded: Never doubt the Woz.

item.title: How to find a Stunt Party event in Forza Horizon 6
item.content:encoded: Completing the Welcome to the Party, Pal! challenge is easier said than done.

item.title: The EFortune Cookie is an adorable e-paper fortune-telling device and I really want to give it a bite
item.content:encoded: Shake it to wake it.

item.title: It's Lenovo a-go-go as the company is responsible for nearly 1 in 4 of all PCs shipped worldwide
item.content:encoded: I don't often apologise for a headline, but in this case I feel like I should.

item.title: An Arc Raiders player who's 'sick of hearing about PvE' has come up with a 'Rival Gangs' PvP mode, and it sounds sick
item.content:encoded: You've piqued my interest.

item.title: How to earn Speed Skills in Forza Horizon 6
item.content:encoded: The Floor It and Gazoo Racer challenges both require you to go fast.

item.title: Where to find the Hakone Nanamagari touge race in Forza Horizon 6, and my tips to win it
item.content:encoded: Tune up your Toyota GR86 for the winding roads.

item.title: Riot taunts would-be hackers using physical hardware to cheat: 'congrats to the owners of a brand new $6k paperweight'
item.content:encoded: Vanguard gets a DMA-spanking upgrade.

item.title: Subnautica 2 could become a chilling horror game, if only it would shut up
item.content:encoded: The abyss should not be this chatty.

item.title: 'What we’re building is grounded in consent, credit, and compensation for the artists and songwriters that take part': Planned Spotify AI tool can generate remixes and covers
item.content:encoded: I'm not really feeling this beat.

item.title: 3 years on from laying off over 1,000 people, Hasbro and Wizards of the Coast are sending daily emails and physical letters encouraging the survivors to not unionise
item.content:encoded: Hey, at least the Pinkertons aren't involved yet.

item.title: Dying Light's former director believes devs are obligated 'to focus and listen to the players' because as soon as a game's released 'it stops being only your game'
item.content:encoded: 60% of the time, it works every time.

item.title: Intel's freshly leaked roadmap for desktop and laptop CPUs is so complicated that it's given me a headache, but at least it all looks very promising on the Core Ultra processor front
item.content:encoded: Unified cores, the return of HyperThreading, and one socket across three generations.

item.title: Where to find the Ohtani region Treasure Hunt in Forza Horizon 6
item.content:encoded: Tick off this Festival Playlist Treasure Hunt challenge.

item.title: The US government is pumping $2,000,000,000 in CHIPS and Science Act money into quantum computing firms
item.content:encoded: A quantum leap. That's too old of a reference, isn't it?

item.title: Destiny developers reflect on the end of an era: 'We all worked so hard to maintain the quality bar under unrealistic constraints'
item.content:encoded: "I logged in to the Tower and found a horde of guardians kneeling by Zavala, others saluting. It was like that from server to server."

item.title: Ubisoft has staff for '70 Warhorse-sized studios' after cuts, says Kingdom Come director—'That could be 10 KCD2-sized games… released every year'
item.content:encoded: That might be too many KCD2-sized games, even for me.

item.title: If this breakdown of the full cost of producing your favourite graphics card is accurate, then prices for certain GPUs are going to make 64 GB DDR5 kits look cheap
item.content:encoded: The RAMpocalypse is the biggest reason for this, of course, but it's only part of the whole problem.
